newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LIGHTNING BEAT RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LIGHTNING BEAT RANGERS.

text.p: Patrick Poulin scored off a rebound with 2:44 left in the third period to snap a tie as the Tampa Bay Lightning posted their sixth straight win over the New York Rangers, 4-3 on Wednesday.

The Rangers led 3-2 after two periods before Shawn Burr scored a fluke goal 2:29 into the period to tie it. From behind the net, Burr centred a pass in front that deflected off Rangers rookie Christian Dube's skate and past Richter for his ninth goal.
Brian Leetch, Mark Messier and Alexei Kovalev scored for New York.

At New Jersey, Rene Corbet scored with 13:05 left in the third period and the undermanned Colorado Avalanche extended their unbeaten streak to eight games by rallying for a 1-1 tie with the New Jersey Devils.
Former Devil Craig Billington made 32 saves for the Avalanche. Colorado played without injured regulars Joe Sakic, Peter Forsberg, Valeri Kamensky, Mike Ricci, Sylvain Lefebvre and Alexei Gusarov.

"We don't have Joey (Sakic) and Peter (Forsberg) and you can go through the whole list," Billington said, "but at the same time I think it's a great compliment to the players who aren't in the lineup all the time and the players who have been brought up from (the minors)."
In Chicago, Jeff Hackett made 35 saves and Tony Amonte scored twice as the Chicago Blackhawks beat the Edmonton Oilers 4-1.
Kevin Miller had three assists and Murray Craven added a pair for Chicago.
Mats Lindgren scored his fifth goal in the third period, spoiling Hackett's chance for a shutout.

In Dallas, Dave Reid recorded his second career hat trick and added an assist for four points and Todd Harvey had a goal and two assists, leading the Dallas Stars to a 6-3 victory over the slumping Detroit Red Wings.
Reid scored his first goal of the game with 2:23 left in the second period to snap a tie and give Dallas a 3-2 lead.
Bob Bassen and Joe Nieuwendyk also scored for the Stars.
At Anaheim, Guy Hebert made 30 saves and Teemu Selanne, Steve Rucchin and Warren Rychel scored first-period goals, giving the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim a 3-2 victory over the Florida Panthers.
Bill Lindsay and rookie David Nemirovsky scored for the Panthers.
